# dua (Disk Usage Analyzer)

**dua** is a tool to conveniently learn about the usage of disk space of a given directory. It's parallel by default and will max out your SSD, providing relevant information as fast as possible. Optionally delete superfluous data, and do so more quickly than `rm`.

[![asciicast](https://asciinema.org/a/kDnXUOeqBxZVMoWuFNqzfpeey.svg)](https://asciinema.org/a/kDnXUOeqBxZVMoWuFNqzfpeey)

## Installation

### Binary Release 

#### MacOS

```sh
curl -LSfs https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Byron/dua-cli/master/ci/install.sh | \
    sh -s -- --git Byron/dua-cli --crate dua --tag v2.29.0
```

#### MacOS via [MacPorts](https://www.macports.org):
```sh
sudo port selfupdate
sudo port install dua-cli
```

#### MacOS via [Homebrew](https://brew.sh)
```sh
brew update
brew install dua-cli
```

#### Linux

Linux requires the target to be specified explicitly to obtain the MUSL build.

```sh
curl -LSfs https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Byron/dua-cli/master/ci/install.sh | \
    sh -s -- --git Byron/dua-cli --target x86_64-unknown-linux-musl --crate dua --tag v2.29.0
```

#### Windows via [Scoop](https://scoop.sh/)
```sh
scoop install dua
```

#### Windows via [WinGet](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/windows/package-manager/winget/)
```sh
winget install Byron.dua-cli
```

#### Pre-built Binaries

See the [releases section](https://github.com/Byron/dua-cli/releases) for manual installation of a binary, pre-built for many platforms.

#### VoidLinux
Via `xbps` on your VoidLinux system.

```
xbps-install dua-cli
```

#### Fedora
Via `dnf` on your Fedora system.

```
sudo dnf install dua-cli
```

#### Arch Linux
Via `pacman` on your ArchLinux system.

```
sudo pacman -S dua-cli
```

#### NixOS
https://search.nixos.org/packages?channel=23.11&show=dua&from=0&size=50&sort=relevance&type=packages&query=dua

Nix-shell (temporary)

```
nix-shell -p dua
```

NixOS configuration

```
  environment.systemPackages = [
    pkgs.dua
  ];
```

#### NetBSD
Via `pkgin` on your NetBSD system.

```
pkgin install dua-cli
```

Or, building from source

```
cd /usr/pkgsrc/sysutils/dua-cli
make install
```

#### Windows

You will find pre-built binaries for Windows in the [releases section](https://github.com/Byron/dua-cli/releases).

#### x-cmd

[x-cmd](https://www.x-cmd.com/) is a **toolbox for Posix Shell**, offering a lightweight package manager built using shell and awk.
```sh
x env use dua
```
- Additionally, the [`x dua ...`](https://www.x-cmd.com/pkg/dua#dua) command is available, which automatically installs `dua` without affecting the environment, such as not modifying the `PATH` variable.

## Usage

```bash
# count the space used in the current working directory
dua
# count the space used in all directories that are not hidden
dua *
# learn about additional functionality
dua aggregate --help
```

### Interactive Mode

Launch into interactive mode with the `i` or `interactive` subcommand. Get help on keyboard
shortcuts with `?`.
Use this mode to explore, and/or to delete files and directories to release disk space.

Please note that great care has been taken to prevent accidental deletions due to a multi-stage
process, which makes this mode viable for exploration.

```bash
dua i
dua interactive
```

## Limitations

* Does not show symbolic links at all if no path is provided when invoking `dua`
  * in an effort to skip symbolic links, for now there are pruned and are not used as a root. Symbolic links will be shown if they
    are not a traversal root, but will not be followed.
* Interactive mode only looks good in dark terminals (see [this issue](https://github.com/Byron/dua-cli/issues/13))
* File names in main window are not truncated if too large. They are cut off on the right.
* There are plenty of examples in test fixtures which don't render correctly in interactive mode.
  This can be due to graphemes not interpreted correctly. With Chinese characters for instance,
  column sizes are not correctly computed, leading to certain columns not being shown.
  In other cases, the terminal gets things wrong - I use alacritty, and with certain characters it
  performs worse than, say iTerm3.
* In interactive mode, you will need about 60MB of memory for 1 million entries in the graph.
* In interactive mode, the maximum amount of files is limited to 2^32 - 1 entries.

## Similar Programs 

* **CLI:**
  * `du`
  * [`dust`](https://github.com/bootandy/dust)
  * [`dutree`](https://github.com/nachoparker/dutree)
  * [`pdu`](https://github.com/KSXGitHub/parallel-disk-usage)
* **TUI:**
  * [`ncdu`](https://dev.yorhel.nl/ncdu)
  * [`gdu`](https://github.com/dundee/gdu)
  * [`godu`](https://github.com/viktomas/godu)
* **GUI:**
  * [GNOME's Disk Usage Analyzer, a.k.a. `baobab`](https://wiki.gnome.org/action/show/Apps/DiskUsageAnalyzer)
  * [Filelight](https://apps.kde.org/filelight/)
</output>

You will find pre-built binaries for Windows in the [releases section](https://github.com/Byron/dua-cli/releases).

#### x-cmd

[x-cmd](https://www.x-cmd.com/) is a **toolbox for Posix Shell**, offering a lightweight package manager built using shell and awk.
```sh
x env use dua
```
- Additionally, the [`x dua ...`](https://www.x-cmd.com/pkg/dua#dua) command is available, which automatically installs `dua` without affecting the environment, such as not modifying the `PATH` variable.

## Usage

```bash
# count the space used in the current working directory
dua
# count the space used in all directories that are not hidden
dua *
# learn about additional functionality
dua aggregate --help
```

### Interactive Mode

Launch into interactive mode with the `i` or `interactive` subcommand. Get help on keyboard
shortcuts with `?`.
Use this mode to explore, and/or to delete files and directories to release disk space.

Please note that great care has been taken to prevent accidental deletions due to a multi-stage
process, which makes this mode viable for exploration.

```bash
dua i
dua interactive
```

## Limitations

* Does not show symbolic links at all if no path is provided when invoking `dua`
  * in an effort to skip symbolic links, for now there are pruned and are not used as a root. Symbolic links will be shown if they
    are not a traversal root, but will not be followed.
* Interactive mode only looks good in dark terminals (see [this issue](https://github.com/Byron/dua-cli/issues/13))
* File names in main window are not truncated if too large. They are cut off on the right.
* There are plenty of examples in test fixtures which don't render correctly in interactive mode.
  This can be due to graphemes not interpreted correctly. With Chinese characters for instance,
  column sizes are not correctly computed, leading to certain columns not being shown.
  In other cases, the terminal gets things wrong - I use alacritty, and with certain characters it
  performs worse than, say iTerm3.
* In interactive mode, you will need about 60MB of memory for 1 million entries in the graph.
* In interactive mode, the maximum amount of files is limited to 2^32 - 1 entries.

## Similar Programs 

* **CLI:**
  * `du`
  * [`dust`](https://github.com/bootandy/dust)
  * [`dutree`](https://github.com/nachoparker/dutree)
  * [`pdu`](https://github.com/KSXGitHub/parallel-disk-usage)
* **TUI:**
  * [`ncdu`](https://dev.yorhel.nl/ncdu)
  * [`gdu`](https://github.com/dundee/gdu)
  * [`godu`](https://github.com/viktomas/godu)
* **GUI:**
  * [GNOME's Disk Usage Analyzer, a.k.a. `baobab`](https://wiki.gnome.org/action/show/Apps/DiskUsageAnalyzer)
  * [Filelight](https://apps.kde.org/filelight/)

fn walk_dir_recursive(
    path: &Path,
    apparent_size: bool,
    count_hard_links: bool,
    ignore_dirs: &HashSet<PathBuf>,
    stay_on_filesystem: bool,
    seen_inodes: &mut HashMap<(u64, u64), u64>,
    results: &mut Vec<(String, u64)>,
    root_device: Option<u64>,
    depth: usize,
) -> u64 {
    let mut total = 0u64;

    let mut entries = match fs::read_dir(path) {
        Ok(entries) => entries.collect::<Vec<_>>(),
        Err(_) => return 0,
    };

    // Sort entries by name
    entries.sort_by(|a, b| {
        let name_a = a.as_ref().ok().and_then(|e| e.file_name().to_str().map(|s| s.to_string())).unwrap_or_default();
        let name_b = b.as_ref().ok().and_then(|e| e.file_name().to_str().map(|s| s.to_string())).unwrap_or_default();
        name_a.cmp(&name_b)
    });

    for entry_result in entries {
        let entry = match entry_result {
            Ok(e) => e,
            Err(_) => continue,
        };

        let entry_path = entry.path();

        // Check if we should ignore this directory
        if let Ok(canonical) = entry_path.canonicalize() {
            if ignore_dirs.contains(&canonical) {
                continue;
            }
        }

        let metadata = match entry.metadata() {
            Ok(m) => m,
            Err(_) => continue,
        };

        // Handle filesystem boundary
        if stay_on_filesystem {
            if let Some(root_dev) = root_device {
                if metadata.dev() != root_dev {
                    continue;
                }
            }
        }

        let mut size = get_size(&metadata, apparent_size);

        // Handle hard links
        if !count_hard_links && metadata.nlink() > 1 {
            let inode_key = (metadata.dev(), metadata.ino());
            if let Some(_) = seen_inodes.get(&inode_key) {
                size = 0;
            } else {
                seen_inodes.insert(inode_key, size);
            }
        } else if !count_hard_links {
            let inode_key = (metadata.dev(), metadata.ino());
            seen_inodes.insert(inode_key, size);
        }

        total += size;

        if depth == 0 {
            if let Some(name) = entry_path.file_name() {
                if let Some(name_str) = name.to_str() {
                    results.push((name_str.to_string(), size));
                }
            }
        }

        if metadata.is_dir() {
            total += walk_dir_recursive(
                &entry_path,
                apparent_size,
                count_hard_links,
                ignore_dirs,
                stay_on_filesystem,
                seen_inodes,
                results,
                root_device,
                depth + 1,
            );
        }
    }

    total
}

fn aggregate_path(
    path: &PathBuf,
    apparent_size: bool,
    count_hard_links: bool,
    ignore_dirs: &HashSet<PathBuf>,
    stay_on_filesystem: bool,
) -> (u64, Vec<(String, u64)>) {
    let metadata = match fs::metadata(path) {
        Ok(m) => m,
        Err(_) => return (0, Vec::new()),
    };

    if metadata.is_file() {
        let size = get_size(&metadata, apparent_size);
        let name = path.file_name()
            .and_then(|n| n.to_str())
            .unwrap_or("")
            .to_string();
        return (size, vec![(name, size)]);
    }

    let mut results = Vec::new();
    let mut seen_inodes = HashMap::new();
    let root_device = if stay_on_filesystem {
        Some(metadata.dev())
    } else {
        None
    };

    let total = walk_dir_recursive(
        path,
        apparent_size,
        count_hard_links,
        ignore_dirs,
        stay_on_filesystem,
        &mut seen_inodes,
        &mut results,
        root_device,
        0,
    );

    // Results are already sorted by name from walk_dir_recursive

    (total, results)
}

fn parse_args() -> (Vec<PathBuf>, String, bool, bool, bool, Vec<PathBuf>, Option<String>, Option<String>) {
    let args: Vec<String> = env::args().collect();
    
    let mut inputs = Vec::new();
    let mut threads = 0;
    let mut format = "binary".to_string();
    let mut apparent_size = false;
    let mut count_hard_links = false;
    let mut stay_on_filesystem = false;
    let mut ignore_dirs = vec![
        PathBuf::from("/proc"),
        PathBuf::from("/dev"),
        PathBuf::from("/sys"),
        PathBuf::from("/run"),
    ];
    let mut log_file = None;
    let mut command = None;
    let mut command_arg = None;

    let mut i = 1;
    while i < args.len() {
        let arg = &args[i];

        match arg.as_str() {
            "--version" | "-V" => {
                println!("dua 2.32.2");
                std::process::exit(0);
            },
            "--help" | "-h" => {
                print_help();
                std::process::exit(0);
            },
            "-t" | "--threads" => {
                i += 1;
                if i < args.len() {
                    threads = args[i].parse().unwrap_or(0);
                }
            },
            "-f" | "--format" => {
                i += 1;
                if i < args.len() {
                    format = args[i].clone();
                }
            },
            "-A" | "--apparent-size" => {
                apparent_size = true;
            },
            "-l" | "--count-hard-links" => {
                count_hard_links = true;
            },
            "-x" | "--stay-on-filesystem" => {
                stay_on_filesystem = true;
            },
            "-i" | "--ignore-dirs" => {
                i += 1;
                ignore_dirs.clear();
                while i < args.len() && !args[i].starts_with('-') {
                    ignore_dirs.push(PathBuf::from(&args[i]));
                    i += 1;
                }
                i -= 1;
            },
            "--log-file" => {
                i += 1;
                if i < args.len() {
                    log_file = Some(args[i].clone());
                }
            },
            "interactive" | "i" => {
                command = Some("interactive".to_string());
                i += 1;
                while i < args.len() && !args[i].starts_with('-') {
                    inputs.push(PathBuf::from(&args[i]));
                    i += 1;
                }
                i -= 1;
            },
            "aggregate" | "a" => {
                command = Some("aggregate".to_string());
                i += 1;
                while i < args.len() && !args[i].starts_with('-') {
                    inputs.push(PathBuf::from(&args[i]));
                    i += 1;
                }
                i -= 1;
            },
            "completions" => {
                i += 1;
                if i < args.len() {
                    command_arg = Some(args[i].clone());
                    command = Some("completions".to_string());
                }
            },
            _ => {
                if !arg.starts_with('-') {
                    inputs.push(PathBuf::from(arg));
                }
            }
        }
        i += 1;
    }

    (inputs, format, apparent_size, count_hard_links, stay_on_filesystem, ignore_dirs, command, command_arg)
}

Usage: dua [FLAGS] [OPTIONS] [SUBCOMMAND] [INPUT]...

Commands:

  aggregate    Aggregate the consumed space of one or more directories or files [aliases: a]

Arguments:

Options:

          [default: binary]
          [possible values: metric, binary, bytes, gb, gib, mb, mib]

          Count hard-linked files each time they are seen

fn main() {
    let (inputs, format, apparent_size, count_hard_links, stay_on_filesystem, ignore_dirs, command, command_arg) = parse_args();

    match command.as_deref() {
        Some("interactive") => {
            eprintln!("Error: Interactive mode requires a connected terminal");
            std::process::exit(1);
        },
        Some("completions") => {
            if let Some(shell) = command_arg {
                generate_completions(&shell);
            }
        },
        _ => {
            // Aggregate mode (default)
            let final_inputs = if inputs.is_empty() {
                // Get all entries in current directory
                let mut entries = Vec::new();
                if let Ok(dir) = fs::read_dir(".") {
                    for entry in dir.filter_map(|e| e.ok()) {
                        entries.push(entry.path());
                    }
                }
                entries
            } else {
                inputs
            };

            let mut ignore_dirs_set = HashSet::new();
            for dir in &ignore_dirs {
                if let Ok(canonical) = dir.canonicalize() {
                    ignore_dirs_set.insert(canonical);
                }
            }

            if final_inputs.len() == 1 {
                let path = &final_inputs[0];
                let (total, entries) = aggregate_path(
                    path,
                    apparent_size,
                    count_hard_links,
                    &ignore_dirs_set,
                    stay_on_filesystem,
                );

                for (name, size) in entries {
                    let formatted = format_bytes(size, &format);
                    println!("{} {}", green(&formatted), name);
                }

                let total_formatted = format_bytes(total, &format);
                println!("{} {}", green(&total_formatted), "total");
            } else if final_inputs.len() > 1 {
                // Handle multiple inputs
                let mut results = Vec::new();
                for input_path in &final_inputs {
                    let (_, entries) = aggregate_path(
                        input_path,
                        apparent_size,
                        count_hard_links,
                        &ignore_dirs_set,
                        stay_on_filesystem,
                    );

                    for (_, size) in entries {
                        results.push((input_path.display().to_string(), size));
                    }
                }

                results.sort_by(|a, b| a.0.cmp(&b.0));

                let mut total = 0u64;
                for (name, size) in &results {
                    let formatted = format_bytes(*size, &format);
                    println!("{} {}", green(&formatted), name);
                    total += size;
                }

                let total_formatted = format_bytes(total, &format);
                println!("{} {}", green(&total_formatted), "total");
            }
        },
    }
}

fn parse_args() -> (Vec<PathBuf>, String, bool, bool, bool, Vec<PathBuf>, Option<String>, Option<String>) {
    let args: Vec<String> = env::args().collect();
    
    let mut inputs = Vec::new();
    let mut threads = 0;
    let mut format = "binary".to_string();
    let mut apparent_size = false;
    let mut count_hard_links = false;
    let mut stay_on_filesystem = false;
    let mut ignore_dirs = vec![
        PathBuf::from("/proc"),
        PathBuf::from("/dev"),
        PathBuf::from("/sys"),
        PathBuf::from("/run"),
    ];
    let mut log_file = None;
    let mut command = None;
    let mut command_arg = None;

    let mut i = 1;
    while i < args.len() {
        let arg = &args[i];

        match arg.as_str() {
            "--version" | "-V" => {
                println!("dua 2.32.2");
                std::process::exit(0);
            },
            "--help" | "-h" => {
                print_help();
                std::process::exit(0);
            },
            "-t" | "--threads" => {
                i += 1;
                if i < args.len() {
                    threads = args[i].parse().unwrap_or(0);
                }
            },
            "-f" | "--format" => {
                i += 1;
                if i < args.len() {
                    format = args[i].clone();
                }
            },
            "-A" | "--apparent-size" => {
                apparent_size = true;
            },
            "-l" | "--count-hard-links" => {
                count_hard_links = true;
            },
            "-x" | "--stay-on-filesystem" => {
                stay_on_filesystem = true;
            },
            "-i" | "--ignore-dirs" => {
                i += 1;
                ignore_dirs.clear();
                while i < args.len() && !args[i].starts_with('-') {
                    ignore_dirs.push(PathBuf::from(&args[i]));
                    i += 1;
                }
                i -= 1;
            },
            "--log-file" => {
                i += 1;
                if i < args.len() {
                    log_file = Some(args[i].clone());
                }
            },
            "interactive" | "i" => {
                command = Some("interactive".to_string());
                i += 1;
                while i < args.len() && !args[i].starts_with('-') {
                    inputs.push(PathBuf::from(&args[i]));
                    i += 1;
                }
                i -= 1;
            },
            "aggregate" | "a" => {
                command = Some("aggregate".to_string());
                i += 1;
                while i < args.len() && !args[i].starts_with('-') {
                    inputs.push(PathBuf::from(&args[i]));
                    i += 1;
                }
                i -= 1;
            },
            "completions" => {
                i += 1;
                if i < args.len() {
                    command_arg = Some(args[i].clone());
                    command = Some("completions".to_string());
                }
            },
            _ => {
                if !arg.starts_with('-') {
                    inputs.push(PathBuf::from(arg));
                }
            }
        }
        i += 1;
    }

    (inputs, format, apparent_size, count_hard_links, stay_on_filesystem, ignore_dirs, command, command_arg)
}

fn main() {
    let (inputs, format, apparent_size, count_hard_links, stay_on_filesystem, ignore_dirs, command, command_arg) = parse_args();

    match command.as_deref() {
        Some("interactive") => {
            eprintln!("Error: Interactive mode requires a connected terminal");
            std::process::exit(1);
        },
        Some("completions") => {
            if let Some(shell) = command_arg {
                generate_completions(&shell);
            }
        },
        _ => {
            // Aggregate mode (default)
            let final_inputs = if inputs.is_empty() {
                // Get all entries in current directory
                let mut entries = Vec::new();
                if let Ok(dir) = fs::read_dir(".") {
                    for entry in dir.filter_map(|e| e.ok()) {
                        entries.push(entry.path());
                    }
                }
                entries
            } else {
                inputs
            };

            let mut ignore_dirs_set = HashSet::new();
            for dir in &ignore_dirs {
                if let Ok(canonical) = dir.canonicalize() {
                    ignore_dirs_set.insert(canonical);
                }
            }

            if final_inputs.len() == 1 {
                let path = &final_inputs[0];
                let (total, entries) = aggregate_path(
                    path,
                    apparent_size,
                    count_hard_links,
                    &ignore_dirs_set,
                    stay_on_filesystem,
                );

                for (name, size) in entries {
                    let formatted = format_bytes(size, &format);
                    println!("{} {}", green(&formatted), name);
                }

                let total_formatted = format_bytes(total, &format);
                println!("{} {}", green(&total_formatted), "total");
            } else if final_inputs.len() > 1 {
                // Handle multiple inputs
                let mut results = Vec::new();
                for input_path in &final_inputs {
                    let (_, entries) = aggregate_path(
                        input_path,
                        apparent_size,
                        count_hard_links,
                        &ignore_dirs_set,
                        stay_on_filesystem,
                    );

                    for (_, size) in entries {
                        results.push((input_path.display().to_string(), size));
                    }
                }

                results.sort_by(|a, b| a.0.cmp(&b.0));

                let mut total = 0u64;
                for (name, size) in &results {
                    let formatted = format_bytes(*size, &format);
                    println!("{} {}", green(&formatted), name);
                    total += size;
                }

                let total_formatted = format_bytes(total, &format);
                println!("{} {}", green(&total_formatted), "total");
            }
        },
    }
}
